directAnswer: Ray tracing can significantly enhance visual fidelity in games, providing realistic lighting and reflections, but it often requires powerful hardware to run effectively.
summary: Ray tracing technology offers a more immersive gaming experience through improved graphics, but the performance cost can be substantial depending on the hardware used.

sections.heading: Performance Impact
sections.body: Enabling ray tracing can lead to a noticeable decrease in frame rates, especially on mid-range GPUs. Users may need to balance settings between ray tracing and performance.

sections.heading: Hardware Requirements
sections.body: To fully utilize ray tracing, a compatible GPU such as NVIDIA's RTX series or AMD's RX 6000 series is recommended. Lower-end GPUs may struggle to maintain playable frame rates.

sections.heading: Game Support
sections.body: Not all games support ray tracing. Popular titles like 'Cyberpunk 2077' and 'Control' offer ray tracing features, while others may not, so check game specifications before purchasing.

steps.title: Check GPU Compatibility
steps.detail: Ensure your GPU supports ray tracing. For NVIDIA, check for RTX branding; for AMD, look for RX 6000 series or later.

steps.title: Enable Ray Tracing in Game Settings
steps.detail: In supported games, navigate to the graphics settings menu and toggle the ray tracing option. Exact paths may vary by game.

steps.title: Adjust Graphics Settings
steps.detail: If performance drops, consider lowering other graphics settings like texture quality or resolution to maintain a smooth experience.

faqs.question: Can I run ray tracing on older GPUs?
faqs.answer: Older GPUs typically do not support ray tracing. You would need a newer model that specifically includes this technology.

faqs.question: Does ray tracing affect gameplay performance?
faqs.answer: Yes, enabling ray tracing can reduce frame rates, which may affect gameplay, especially in fast-paced titles.

faqs.question: Are there any games that don't support ray tracing?
faqs.answer: Yes, many games still do not support ray tracing. Always check the game's specifications or official announcements for details.

caveats: Ray tracing can significantly increase power consumption and heat output, potentially leading to thermal throttling in some systems.
